subject: Locational TTL redlines and backup residency — coordination
messages:
From: Sofia Mendez <sofia.m@acme-analytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jake Turner <jake.turner@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Apr 2028 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Locational TTL and backup residency questions

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Friday. Our legal team ran the DPA appendix you sent and surfaced a few open items we need clarified before we can approve the retention/deletion language:

- Backups: the redline currently allows backups to be retained for up to 180 days with geographic fallback. Can you confirm whether backup replicas can be restricted to EU-only storage and whether we can require certified deletion of onshore backup copies within 30 days of a customer erasure request?
- Cache/ephemeral data: we need clearer language around embeddings/serving KV caches (what you earlier called "ephemeral TTL"). Acme’s policy is <=30 days for any customer-identifiable transient state — are you able to commit to a 30 day TTL for customer-specific prefixes and a documented purge process?
- Proof: what evidence package does Redwood provide for deletion from cold backups? We usually require a deletion certificate and audit log excerpt.

I've attached our suggested redline in track-changes (legal@acme also included). Happy to jump on a short call if it's easier.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Mendez
Head of Legal Ops, Acme Analytics

Attachment: Acme_DPA_redline_20280429.docx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Mendez <sofia.m@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jake Turner <jake.turner@acme-analytics.com>, legal@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 30 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Locational TTL and backup residency questions

Sofia — appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers up front, and then details below.

High level proposals we think will address Acme's risk profile:
- Backups: main/primary data and backups can be geo-restricted to EU regions for your tenant. For onshore backup certification we can commit to performing and providing deletion evidence for affected onshore replicas within 45 days of a validated erasure request; we can explore a 30-day target for a localized SLA in the final schedule if Acme signs the dedicated retention appendix.
- Ephemeral caches: we can set customer-specific KV prefixes to a default TTL of 30 days and include a documented purge API for forced eviction; we will include this as an operational appendix.
- Proof package: we'll provide a deletion certificate that includes job id, timestamp, replica identifiers, and an audit log extract showing the erasure steps. For cold snap/archival media, we provide an attestation that the snapshot has been marked for policy-based purge and evidence of the subsequent purge job run.

Details / tradeoffs:
- Why 45 days for backups: cross-region restore windows + retention for disaster recovery mean an operational window to validate any restore dependencies; 45 days is our standard compromise without a dedicated capacity commitment. If Acme elects a Dedicated plan (reserved capacity + onshore-only backup mirrors) we can scope a 30-day certified deletion commitment in the appendix and add an SLA credit if missed.
- Ephemeral caches will not be backed up in long-term archival by default. We will document exactly which indices are snapshot/backup-eligible.

I've attached our redline (Redwood_DPA_redline_20280430.docx) and a retention TTL table for the Acme tenant. Can Marissa or Stephanie weigh in on whether legal is comfortable with the 45 -> 30 day trade path (Dedicated upgrade triggers)?

If that looks OK, I'll propose a short working call Wednesday to lock language and agree on the DocuSign timeline.

Cheers,
Aditya
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_redline_20280430.docx; Retention_TTL_table_20280430.xlsx

From: legal@acme-analytics.com
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Sofia Mendez <sofia.m@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Jake Turner <jake.turner@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Locational TTL and backup residency questions

On Tue, 01 May 2028 09:12, legal@acme-analytics.com wrote:

Thanks for the rapid response, Aditya. A couple follow-ups from a legal perspective:

1) Deletion SLA: Acme cannot accept a firm requirement to upgrade to Dedicated to get the 30-day deletion SLA. Can Redwood accept the 30-day certified deletion from onshore backup replicas as a contractual baseline for EU customers? If not, we need explicit, granular language describing the conditions that would justify a longer window.

2) Forensic evidence: the deletion certificate you propose is good, but we need an example template and a sample audit-log extract (redacted is fine) to verify the fields and format.

3) Escrow/independent attestation: would Redwood consider a quarterly third-party attestation (or allowing an Acme-appointed auditor once per year) to validate the deletion procedures for a production tenant? We understand cost-sharing may be required — please propose options.

Please mark up the redline and we'll get back quickly.

Regards,
Acme Legal

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: legal@acme-analytics.com, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Locational TTL and backup residency questions

Hi all — Stephanie from Redwood Legal. Quick notes on the legal position and a proposed redline approach:

- Baseline: Redwood can accept a 30-day certified deletion obligation for onshore backup replicas limited to customer-specific replicas that are not required for cross-tenant disaster recovery. We need to preserve limited operational carve-outs (admin discovery window, legal holds from law enforcement) and will add explicit language about exceptions and notice obligations.
- Audit package: attaching a sample deletion certificate template (we'll include job id, replica id, start/end timestamps, operator id, and a hash of the deleted manifest). We can produce a redacted audit-log extract on request.
- Attestation: we can offer an annual third-party attestation for an additional compliance addendum (cost to be discussed). Alternatively, we can offer a quarterly internal attestation plus annual independent audit if Acme prefers.

Proposed next step: we prepared a short appendix text that accepts 30-day certified deletion for EU onshore backup replicas with the listed operational exceptions and describes the proof artifacts. I've pushed a draft to DocuSign for fast signature once you accept the wording: https://www.docusign.com/templates/rdw-dpa-appendix-2028

If acceptable, Aditya, please coordinate a 30-minute scoping call so engineering can confirm the purge job IDs and sample audit extract timeframe. Laura — can you own scheduling and get engineering on the line?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Deletion_Certificate_template_20280430.docx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Mendez <sofia.m@acme-analytics.com>, legal@acme-analytics.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Locational TTL and backup residency questions

Great — sounds like we're converging. Next steps from Redwood:

1) Engineering will produce a redacted audit-log extract and the deletion-certificate sample by EOD Monday (attachments: Retention_TTL_table_20280430.xlsx + sample certificate).
2) Legal will post the suggested appendix to DocuSign. If Acme accepts the appendix we will treat the 30-day certified deletion as contractual baseline for your tenant restricted to EU onshore replicas, with the operational exceptions discussed.
3) I'll set a 30-min call Monday to walk the Acme team through the purge job lifecycle and show the certificate fields. Laura will propose two times.

If anything is missing, flag it here. Otherwise, Sofia — can you confirm Acme's preference on annual independent audit vs quarterly internal attestation so we can include it in the appendix?

Thanks,
Aditya
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
